paras: The burning of the Black church at Cedar Grove, Alabama, was an arson attack on the church of a Black congregation at Cedar Grove, Bibb County, by persons described as 'white incendiaries', reported in early July 1881. According to the same report, Black incendiaries burned the white church the next night, and the pairing of the two fires was the whole of the story as it circulated in newspaper news-summary columns.

The earliest version found, in the Hopkinsville South Kentuckian of July 12, 1881, said that 'a negro church at cedar Grove Bibb county, Ala, was burned recently by white incendiaries.' It added that 'the next night negro incendiaries burned the white church.' No exact date, names, number of incendiaries or source for their identification appears in any version.
No report of arrests, an investigation or rebuilding appears in the coverage.

The item ran only as a single sentence in columns of miscellaneous news, alongside notices of drownings, fires and curiosities. The Dallas Daily Herald printed a slightly reworded version on July 13, and the same wording appeared in the 'News Gleanings' column of the Winchester, Tennessee, Home Journal on July 20. The same gleanings text reappeared word for word in the Pickens Sentinel of South Carolina on July 21 and the Magnolia Gazette of Mississippi on July 22.

The Vermont Watchman and State Journal rewrote the item for its 'Weekly News Summary' on July 20, dropping the county and saying that 'black incendiaries retaliated on the white church.' None of the papers added a headline, a source or any comment on either fire.

accounts.label: Wire / news-summary brief
accounts.gist: White incendiaries recently burned the negro church at Cedar Grove, Bibb County, Alabama; the next night black incendiaries burned the white church.

accounts.label: Vermont Watchman rewording
accounts.gist: Gives the first fire as 'the other night' and says the black incendiaries 'retaliated' on the white church.

framing.detail: Printed without headline or comment as one item among unrelated news gleanings, the two church burnings stated as a matched pair.
The Vermont Watchman cast the second fire as retaliation ('retaliated on the white church'), placing it just below a joke item about a drunk who 'retaliated' on a snake.
